A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multifidelity simulation-based inference work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and neuroscience simulation results, posterior checks, transfer-learning analyses and computational-cost measurements, including Figs. 2–3 and Table 4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds Gaussian-target inference, spiking-network dimensionality ablations and TARP calibration results in Figs. 9, 19 and 22.

M1.justification: v4 Appendix D.4 introduces an adaptation for a low-fidelity model with more parameters: retain its extra dimension as a dummy, fine-tune on high-fidelity dimensions and restrict posterior evaluation accordingly. The core algorithms remain unchanged; A-MF-TSNPE is renamed MF-TSNPE-AF.

E1.justification: v4 adds a Gaussian-target inference scenario pretrained on a three-parameter OU model, testing low-fidelity dimensionality greater than high-fidelity dimensionality (Appendix D.4). The six principal tasks are retained; the spiking-network dimensionality ablation stays within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal NPE, TSNPE and MF-ABC baselines remain. However, the L5PC calibration comparison in Fig. 3C adds an AF-variant curve, labeled 'TARP MF-NPE5-AF', alongside NPE and MF-NPE5. Renaming the active sequential method alone does not introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce TARP coverage diagnostics and three- and six-parameter low-fidelity spiking-model settings. Separately, the retained perturbation experiment changes its stated construction from sigma plus Gaussian epsilon in v3 Appendix B.1 to sigma plus delta in v4 Sec. 4.4. This establishes a reporting change, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands validation through the reversed-dimensionality test, a spiking-network ablation exposing negative transfer, and TARP calibration across all six principal tasks. The earlier noise/reversal analysis is moved into Sec. 4.4, and the existing simulation-based calibration remains in Appendix F.2.

E5.justification: v4 newly reports 200 runs for the TARP calibration test (Fig. 22) and uncertainty on the L5PC cost-reduction summary, 4.44 ± 0.06 instead of '4–5 times'. Existing network-initialization counts and confidence-interval practices are retained; increased training repetitions are not established.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include improved inference in the Gaussian-target test, negative transfer at low high-fidelity budgets with three low-fidelity spiking parameters and 100,000 pretraining samples, and across-task TARP coverage curves. The original benchmark curves and cost/accuracy tables are retained, so these additions do not establish version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The perturbation's formal probabilistic specification changes from sigma + epsilon with epsilon drawn from N(0, delta^2) to sigma + delta, dropping the explicit random draw. The NPE/KL convergence proof, simulator equations and mutual-information invariance argument are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: multifidelity transfer learning for amortized and sequential posterior estimation, uncertainty-guided acquisition, and up to two orders of magnitude fewer high-fidelity simulations at comparable performance. Renaming and added supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds a concrete applicability qualification: increasing parameter mismatch reduces transfer benefits, and extensive pretraining can cause negative transfer in the three-parameter spiking case (Sec. 4.3; Appendix G.3). It also clarifies that acquisition targets epistemic uncertainty within the simulator domain. The mutual-information interpretation was already present in v3.

D1.justification: Sec. 6 changes from promising a future code/data release to reporting public availability with a repository address. v4 also documents the new dummy-dimension procedure and fixed parameter values for the spiking ablation. Existing architecture, optimization and hardware disclosures are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for TARP, truncated ratio estimation and additional multifidelity research, while removing discussion of Bayesian neural networks and learned simulator surrogates. The central positioning around expert-designed low-fidelity simulators and transfer learning remains. The Jaxley publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction and background are streamlined, method acronyms are removed from the abstract, and the active variant is renamed. The former Appendix B discussion is integrated into Sec. 4.4, with corresponding appendix renumbering. Most remaining prose and organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figs. 9, 19 and 22, replaces Fig. 3C with TARP, reformats Fig. 3F, and moves Fig. 4 into the main text. Legends and algorithm formatting are revised. Most existing graphics and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added calibration checks and explicit negative-transfer case strengthen validation and applicability guidance, while the reported code/data access improves reproducibility information. These are useful incremental gains over v3's retained evidence. The unexplained perturbation-specification change alongside unchanged Fig. 4 curves leaves a localized reproducibility ambiguity, limiting the improvement.
